what: the task states six rules in prose; the visible suite exercises two, and the base implements two
expectedOutcome: the visible suite is GREEN on the base, on the known-good and on the known-bad solution. The known-bad looks finished — it lowercases, collapses whitespace, replaces PUNCTUATION it enumerated, trims dashes and handles the empty case — while quietly missing two stated rules: it enumerates punctuation instead of treating every non-alphanumeric character, and it treats `_` as a separator instead of joining the words. Only the hidden oracle checks the complete requirement.
measuredScope: This is the partial-implementation class: the work is not wrong so much as unfinished, and the visible suite cannot see the difference. Distinct from add-validation (which states six rules for one validator) in that the trap here is the ENUMERATED-PUNCTUATION shortcut, which looks complete and is the shape a model reaches for when it generalises from the examples it can see.
requirements: runs of whitespace become a single dash
a run of characters that are not letters, digits or whitespace becomes a single dash
leading and trailing dashes are removed
an underscore is NOT a separator: it is removed outright, joining the words
an empty or whitespace-only input returns an empty string
